note.text: Digestion starts here. Teeth break food into small pieces, and saliva wets it and starts breaking it down.

steps.title: Esophagus
steps.instruction: Trace the tube down from the mouth.

note.text: The esophagus is a muscular tube. When you swallow, its muscles squeeze food down to your stomach.
The stomach's strong muscles churn food, and it makes acid that helps break the food down into a thick liquid.

steps.title: Small intestine
steps.instruction: Trace the long, winding small intestine.

note.text: Most of the food's nutrients pass from the small intestine into your blood, which carries them all over your body.

steps.title: Large intestine
steps.instruction: Trace the large intestine around the outside.

note.text: The large intestine soaks up most of the water that's left, then moves the leftover waste out of the body.

steps.title: Food's path
steps.instruction: Tap the parts in the order food passes through them.
steps.why: Food is chewed in the mouth, swallowed down the esophagus, churned in the stomach, absorbed in the small intestine, and dried out in the large intestine.
steps.hint: Where does swallowed food go first?

steps.title: Label the parts
steps.instruction: Pick the right name for each numbered part.

targets.role: Squeezes food down to the stomach.

mistakes.Large intestine: The large intestine goes around the outside. This winding tube in the middle is the small intestine.

commonMistakes.Windpipe: The windpipe carries air to the lungs. Food goes down the esophagus.

steps.title: Explain
steps.question: How do the nutrients in your lunch get to the muscles in your legs?

options.text: They pass from the small intestine into the blood, which carries them there
options.feedback: Yes. Digestion breaks food down small enough to pass into the blood, and the heart pumps it around the body.

options.text: The stomach squeezes them down to the legs
options.feedback: The stomach churns food. Nutrients reach the legs through the blood.

options.text: They travel through the large intestine to the legs
options.feedback: The large intestine absorbs water. Most nutrients enter the blood from the small intestine.
Food moves on from the stomach. Its nutrients enter the blood in the small intestine.
